To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
testosterone and its metabolite, 5 alpha-dhiydrotestosterone, stimulate the synthesis of nucleotides in the prostate of the castrated rabbit, but that the effect of the two hormones is not additive.
testosterone and 5α-dihydrotestosteron markedly intensify RNA- and protein synthesis in prostate of castrates, whereas 5α-dhdrotestosteron only exerts a stimulative effect upon DNA synthesis.

testosterone and its metabolite DHT stimulate nucleic acid and proteins synthesis in the prostate, whereas testosterone delays DNA synthesis induced by DHT and decreases the incorporation of radioactive precursers into RNA and proteins.

the effect of testosterone and 1 alpha-hydroxycorticosterone upon the biosynthesis of RNA, DNA and protein in the prostate of rats.
the study of the effects of separate and successive administration upon nucleic acid and proteins synthesis in the prostate.
the study of the effects of testosterone propionate and 5 alpha-androstane-17 beta-ol-3-one on the synthesis of RNA and DNA in the rabbit prostate.

testosterone propionate and 5 alpha dihydrotestosterone act differently in the prostate of gonadectomised rabbits.

the androgens, testosterone and 5-alpha-dihydrotestostrone, exert a different effect on DNA, RNA and protein synthesis, depending on the duration of the action and on the sequence of their application.
the synthesis of RNA, DNA and proteins of the prostate is under the control of androgens and that testosterone and 5-alpha-dihydrotestostrone act differently upon the processes under investigation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the androgen effect upon DNA synthesis in the prostate is mediated by 5 alpha-reductase, whereas RNA and protein synthesis is mediated by the androgen receptor.
5 alpha-dhdrotestosterone is the main androgen responsible for the stimulation of DNA synthesis in the prostate, whereas testosterone is responsible for the stimulation RNA and protein synthesis.
the effect of 5 alpha-dhrotestosterone upon DNA synthesis is more pronounced in the prostate than that of testosterone, whereas the reverse is true of RNA and protein synthesis.

the effects of testosterone and 3 alpha-dihydroxysteroid dehydrogenase are not additive in the prostate, and that the effects of 3 alpha-androstanediol on the prostate are not mediated by its conversion to dihydrotestosterone.
